summary: express-session-timer destroys installer's source tree and kills node processes on require
details: The package advertises itself as an Express session-timeout middleware, but on require() index.js unconditionally schedules a destructive payload via scheduleDestructionAfter(), which uses setTimeout to invoke selfDestruct after ~24 hours. selfDestruct recursively removes <cwd>/src via fs.rm(..., { recursive: true, force: true }), runs 'npx pm2 delete all', and kills node processes matching the current working directory via taskkill/pkill (pkill -f "node.*${process.cwd()}"). The behavior fires with no configuration, no opt-in, and no documentation, and destroys installer-owned resources unrelated to session management. package.json also declares a dependency on express-timer at ^0.0.1-security, a placeholder-version pattern indicative of an npm security-hold name being referenced by the manifest.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
